fields.name: Additional conditions

bindings.note: Tag 47A — whole block, kept unparsed for requirement cards

fields.description: Free text conditions added by the applicant or issuing bank.

fields.name: Adverse clausing
fields.description: A clause expressly declaring a defective condition of the goods or packaging, per UCP 600 art. 27. Omitted entirely where the document is clean, because the rule that reads it tests for absence.

bindings.note: UCP 600 art. 27. Copy the clause verbatim — 'three cartons torn', 'drums leaking'. Added stamps and manuscript notes only. Pre-printed exculpatory wording ('said to contain', 'shipper's load and count') is NOT adverse clausing. OMIT THIS FIELD ENTIRELY when the document is clean; do not answer 'none' or 'null'.

bindings.note: Tag 50
Party the invoice is made out to: "buyer", "consignee", "sold to", "bill to"

fields.description: How the credit is available — sight, acceptance, negotiation or deferred payment.

bindings.note: Tag 59 — first line
Issuer of the invoice, however labelled: "seller", "exporter", "shipper", "from"

fields.description: The party in whose favour the credit is issued.

fields.name: Corrections authenticated
fields.description: Whether every correction appears authenticated by the issuer, per ISBP 821 section A. YES, NO, or NA where there is nothing to authenticate.

bindings.note: ISBP 821 §A. Depends on corrections_present: answer NA whenever corrections_present is NO — there is nothing to authenticate, and NO would be read as an unauthenticated correction. Answer YES only if every correction carries the issuer's initials or stamp, NO if any does not.

ISBP 821 §A. Depends on corrections_present: answer NA whenever corrections_present is NO — there is nothing to authenticate, and NO would be read as an unauthenticated correction. Answer YES only if every correction carries the issuer's initials or stamp, NO if any does not.

fields.name: Corrections present
fields.description: Whether any value on the document has been corrected, overwritten or struck through.

bindings.note: Any altered date, quantity, party or port. Pre-printed form text is not a correction.
Any altered amount, tenor or drawee.

fields.name: Credit amount

bindings.note: Tag 32B, widened by the 39A tolerance when present

fields.description: Currency and amount of the credit, with any tolerance.

fields.name: Credit reference

bindings.note: Tag 20 — the sender's reference for this credit.

fields.description: The credit's own number, as the issuing bank assigned it.

bindings.note: Tag 32B — first three characters
Code beside the total

fields.description: Currency denomination of the figure on this document.

fields.name: Documents required

fields.description: Free text listing the documents the credit calls for.

fields.name: Draft tenor

bindings.note: Tag 42C, "drafts at"
The tenor phrase on the face: "at sight", "at 60 days after B/L date"

fields.description: The tenor the draft is drawn at.

fields.name: Drawee

bindings.note: Tag 42A or 42D
Party named after "drawn on" or "to"

fields.description: The party the draft is drawn on.

fields.name: Endorsement present
fields.description: Whether the document carries an endorsement, usually on the reverse — a to-order bill of lading, or an insurance document payable to order.

bindings.note: Check the reverse. A bill consigned 'to order' needs an endorsement; one consigned to a named party does not.
Check the reverse for the drawer's endorsement.

fields.name: Expiry date

bindings.note: Tag 31D — first six digits, YYMMDD. Report eight: 20241231.
Only where the schedule restates it: "valid until", "expires on"

fields.description: The last date documents may be presented under the credit.

fields.name: Freight notation
fields.description: Whether freight is marked prepaid or collect, per UCP 600 art. 26(b). Usually a stamp or a ticked box rather than typed text.

bindings.note: UCP 600 art. 26(b). One of: prepaid, collect, none. Read the stamp or the ticked box, not the printed labels of both options.

fields.name: Goods description

bindings.note: Tag 45A — as written, newlines kept
The description block
The description of packages and goods as printed on the bill.

fields.description: How the goods are described.

bindings.note: Highest-level total: "total", "grand total", "total amount due"; sum the lines if none is shown

fields.description: Total value claimed on the invoice.

fields.name: Issue date

bindings.note: Tag 31C, YYMMDD. Report eight: 20241231.

fields.description: The date the credit was issued.

fields.name: Latest shipment date

bindings.note: Tag 44C, or derived from the 44D shipment period

fields.description: The last date shipment may be effected.

fields.name: Legibility
fields.description: How readable the scan is: clear, partial or poor. Present so that a thin extraction can be explained by the scan rather than read as an absent value.

bindings.note: One of: clear, partial, poor. 'partial' when some region could not be read; name it in the marks.
One of: clear, partial, poor.

fields.name: On-board date

bindings.note: Dated on-board notation; the issue date only where the wording is pre-printed

fields.description: The date the goods were actually shipped.

fields.name: On-board notation
fields.description: Whether the shipped-on-board wording is pre-printed on the form or was added as a dated notation, per UCP 600 art. 20(a)(ii). The two date shipment differently.

bindings.note: UCP 600 art. 20(a)(ii). One of: preprinted, added, none. 'added' means a separate dated on-board notation was stamped or written on; that date is the shipment date, not the issue date.

fields.name: Original or copy
fields.description: What the document says it is, per UCP 600 art. 17: original, duplicate, triplicate, copy, or none where nothing is marked.

bindings.note: UCP 600 art. 17. One of: original, duplicate, triplicate, copy, none. An apparently original signature, mark, stamp or label makes it original even where the word is absent.
UCP 600 art. 17. One of: original, duplicate, triplicate, copy, none.

fields.name: Originals issued
fields.description: How many originals the document itself states were issued — the '3/3' or 'full set of three originals' on a transport document.

bindings.note: UCP 600 art. 20(a)(iv). The number stated in 'number of originals' or a '3/3' notation. Null if the document does not say.

fields.name: Place of expiry

bindings.note: Tag 31D — text following the date

fields.description: The counter at which the credit expires.

fields.name: Place of presentation

bindings.note: 41A / 41D — the bank line before "BY"
The bank and place the documents were lodged with, as the schedule states it

fields.description: Bank and location with which the credit is available.

fields.name: Port of discharge

bindings.note: Tag 44F
"Port of discharge" or "to" — not an inland final destination

fields.description: Where the goods are to be delivered.

fields.name: Port of loading

bindings.note: Tag 44E
"Port of loading" or "from" — the named port, not a place of receipt

fields.description: Where the goods were taken on board.

fields.name: Presentation date

bindings.note: Receipt stamp date, else the date the case was opened

fields.description: The date documents reached the presentation counter.

fields.name: Presentation period

bindings.note: Tag 48; 21 calendar days where the credit is silent

fields.description: Days after shipment within which documents must be presented.

fields.name: Receipt stamp date
fields.description: The date on the presenting bank's receipt stamp. This is the presentation date UCP 600 art. 14(c) is counted against, and it is a stamp rather than typed text.

bindings.note: The date inside the bank's receipt chop, not any typed date on the letter. Eight digits, YYYYMMDD, where the stamp is unambiguous.

fields.name: Seal or chop present
fields.description: Whether an official seal, company chop or embossed stamp appears on the document, distinct from a signature.

bindings.note: The presenting bank's receipt chop.

fields.name: Signature medium
fields.description: How the document was signed: handwritten, facsimile, rubber stamp, embossed, perforated, electronic or printed. Evidence rather than a test — UCP 600 art. 3 accepts all of them.

bindings.note: One of: handwritten, facsimile, rubber stamp, embossed, perforated, electronic, printed.
One of: handwritten, facsimile, rubber stamp, embossed, perforated, electronic, printed.

fields.name: Signed
fields.description: Whether the document carries a signature in any of the forms UCP 600 art. 3 accepts — handwriting, facsimile, perforation, stamp, symbol, or electronic authentication.

bindings.note: UCP 600 art. 20(a)(i). YES if signed in any form art. 3 accepts. A printed carrier chop counts.
Signed by the drawer on the face of the draft.

fields.name: Signed by
fields.description: The name appearing with the signature, as printed. Null where a signature is present but its owner cannot be read.

bindings.note: The name printed with or beneath the signature. Null if present but illegible — that is not the same as unsigned.

fields.name: Signing capacity
fields.description: The capacity the signature was given in, and for an agent the party it acted for. UCP 600 art. 20(a)(i) is not satisfied by a signature that does not state this.

bindings.note: UCP 600 art. 20(a)(i). Copy the capacity as printed: 'as carrier', 'as agent for XYZ Lines, the carrier', 'as master'. Null when the signature names a company and no capacity — that absence is the finding.

fields.name: Tolerance

bindings.note: Tag 39A — the plus percentage. 0 when the tag is absent.

fields.description: The percentage the drawing may exceed the credit amount by.

agents.summary: Validity period, latest shipment date, place of expiry and how the credit is available.
agents.behavior: You read the letter of credit's validity period, latest shipment date, place of expiry and how the credit is available. Flag anything that risks a late or mis-routed presentation. Reason step by step and cite the UCP 600 / ISBP 821 article behind each call.
agents.description: Reads the validity period, shipment timing and availability of the credit — the first things an experienced checker looks at.

agents.name: Transport Documents Review

guidance.expr: SHIPPED ON BOARD, LADEN ON BOARD

agents.summary: Bills of lading, air waybills, multimodal and charter-party documents.
agents.behavior: You examine transport documents — bills of lading, air waybills, multimodal and charter-party. Check loading evidence, on-board dating, ports of loading/discharge and clean status against the credit.
agents.description: Bills of lading, air waybills, multimodal and charter-party documents — loading evidence, dating and ports.

agents.name: Commercial Invoice & Goods
agents.summary: Goods description, amounts and pricing, marks and quantities.
agents.behavior: You check the commercial invoice: the goods description corresponds to the credit, amounts and unit prices sit within tolerance, and marks and quantities are consistent across documents.
agents.description: Commercial invoice — goods description corresponding to the credit, amounts, tolerances and unit prices.

agents.name: Document Set & Conditions Review
agents.summary: The set presented, how it is executed, and what this credit adds in 46A and 47A.
agents.description: Reads the document set against what the credit calls for, the marks that authenticate each page, and the applicant's own conditions.
agents.behavior: You examine the presentation as a set: whether every document the credit calls for is there, whether corrections are authenticated, and whether this credit's own conditions in 46A and 47A are satisfied. A condition naming no document and no data point is non-documentary — report it as a note rather than a discrepancy. Cite the UCP 600 / ISBP 821 article behind each call.

groups.name: The set presented
groups.desc: Whether what the credit calls for is here, and properly executed.

checks.body:
Read {Additional conditions} one condition at a time — numbered items or sentences — and decide what, if anything, evidences each.

- A condition naming a document and something it must show: check that document carries the wording demanded.
- A condition fixing a value — credit number, incoterm, vessel, port — compare it with the field on the documents.
- A condition naming the issuer of a document: check the document was issued by that party.
- A condition setting timing: count from the shipment date, in calendar days unless it says banking days.
- A condition naming no document and no data point is non-documentary. Disregard it for the discrepancy list and report it to the checker as a note.

Where a condition repeats something the credit already requires elsewhere, raise it once, not twice.
checks.title: Additional conditions are satisfied
checks.suggestion: A holding position, and it should not survive. :47A: conditions are whatever THIS credit imposes, so a standing table cannot enumerate them — asked as one question it tells an officer that something in 47A is unevidenced without telling them which. The right answer is a requirement card per condition, minted at plan time, which needs the planner to write tables (docs/plan/agent-rules.md §8 C-2). Until then this is here so 47A is not uncovered, and it answers doubt rather than discrepancy because one unanswered question across N conditions is not grounds for a refusal.

rule.source:
WHEN "every condition stated in the credit's additional conditions is evidenced
      by a document in this presentation"                                       THEN "clean"
ELSE "doubt"

checks.body:
Read the goods description and the named parties across the credit, the invoice and the bill of lading, and decide whether they can all be true of one shipment.

The standard is UCP 600 art. 14(d): data need not be identical, but must not conflict.

- Goods. The invoice description must correspond with the credit (art. 18(c)). A more specific description on the invoice — a model number, a grade, a pack size — corresponds and does not conflict. A transport document may describe the goods in general terms, and general terms that are consistent with the credit do not conflict. What conflicts is goods that cannot be the same goods.
- Parties. A difference in legal form or punctuation is not a conflict: ACME TRADING CO., LTD. and Acme Trading Company Limited are one company. A different company is a conflict.
- Addresses. The party's address need not match, but the country must not differ from what the credit states (art. 14(j)).

Raise one finding per conflict, naming both documents and quoting both readings. Where the two merely differ without conflicting, say so and raise nothing — a difference that matters to nobody is not a discrepancy.
checks.title: Documents do not conflict with each other
checks.suggestion: Was authored as a comparison over four rows, three of which used an operator that is a judgement. The catalogue now derives that and files it here; the wording above is what those rows were reaching for.

rule.source:
WHEN "the goods description, the named parties and the shipment particulars on the
      invoice, the bill of lading and the credit can all be true of one shipment.
      Data need not be identical, but must not conflict — UCP 600 art. 14(d)"   THEN "clean"
ELSE "discrepancy"

rule.scope: Every presentation with a commercial invoice
rule.message: The invoice value exceeds the credit amount, or is in the wrong currency.

checks.title: Invoice value within the credit amount
checks.suggestion: Add a row for unit price against the credit once pricing is extracted.

checks.title: Presented where the credit is available
checks.suggestion: Where the credit is available by mixed payment, each portion wants its own row against the draft that covers it.

rule.message: The documents were presented somewhere other than the place the credit expires, or the credit does not say where it is available.

checks.title: Corrections are authenticated

rule.scope: A bill of lading carrying a correction
rule.message: A correction on the bill of lading is not authenticated by its issuer.

checks.suggestion: ISBP 821 exempts corrections on documents issued by the beneficiary, other than a draft — which is why the invoice and the beneficiary's certificates are not operands. The certificate of origin and the insurance document want the same check; copy this one per document rather than adding rows to it, so an unpresented document does not turn the whole check inconclusive.

checks.title: Transport document signed, with capacity

rule.scope: Any presentation including a bill of lading
rule.message: The bill of lading is unsigned, or the signature does not state the capacity it was given in.

checks.suggestion: A signature naming a company but no capacity — 'ABC Shipping' with no 'as carrier' or 'as agent for' — is the common form of this. UCP 600 art. 3 makes a printed chop a signature, so do not raise this merely because nothing was handwritten.

rule.scope: When a marine bill of lading is presented
rule.message: The bill of lading's ports do not agree with the credit.

checks.title: Bill of lading ports agree with the credit
checks.suggestion: Held four subjects at once. The shipment date moved to SHIP-44C and the twenty-one day presentation period to PRES-14C — the latter was cited as art. 20 here, which does not govern it. Still to add: charter-party bills of lading, which are examined under art. 22.

checks.title: Presented before the credit expired
checks.suggestion:
Expiry is expiry. UCP 600 art. 6(d)(i): documents must be presented on or before the expiry date, and art. 6(d)(ii) makes the place for presentation that of the bank with which the credit is available — so the covering schedule's date IS the counter date, and there is no transit to allow for. Nothing here is a matter of degree.

The one thing that can overturn a failure is art. 29(a): where the expiry date falls on a day the bank at the place for presentation is closed, the last day rolls to the first following banking day. We hold no banking calendar for that place, so a presentation one or two days past an expiry that fell on a weekend or holiday may still be compliant — check the calendar before refusing, and note that art. 29(b) requires the covering schedule to state that the presentation was made within the extended period.

WHERE the documents were presented is a different question and belongs to C0002 (Presented where the credit is available). It reads place_of_presentation; note that available_with is the METHOD — sight, acceptance, negotiation, deferred payment — and never the bank.

rule.scope: When a transport document is presented

checks.title: Shipment not later than the credit allows
checks.suggestion: The on-board date is the date of shipment (art. 20(a)(ii)); where the bill carries a separate on-board notation it is that date, not the issuance date, that this reads. Cannot be a threshold check: the bill of lading has to be read before there is anything to compare.

rule.scope: When a transport document is presented
rule.source:
WHEN #absent({LC.presentation_period})
     and #daysBetween({BOL.on_board_date}, {CS.presentation_date}) <= 21   THEN "clean"
WHEN #present({LC.presentation_period})
     and #atMost(#daysBetween({BOL.on_board_date}, {CS.presentation_date}),
                 {LC.presentation_period}, 0)                              THEN "clean"
ELSE "discrepancy"

checks.title: Presented within the presentation period
checks.suggestion: Twenty-one calendar days after the date of shipment unless the credit states its own period, which is why the condition has two branches keyed on whether presentation_period was read. Expiry is NOT tested here — art. 14(c) also requires presentation before expiry, and DATE-31D is where that is answered, so a presentation that is both late and expired is two grounds and not one ground counted twice.

articles.read: A credit must name the bank with which it is available and the way it is available — sight payment, deferred payment, acceptance or negotiation. It must also state an expiry date and the place where documents are to be presented; presentation must be made on or before that date.
articles.title: Availability, expiry date and place for presentation
articles.summary: Where, how and until when the credit may be used.

articles.read: Banks examine documents on their face to decide whether they form a complying presentation, taking up to five banking days. Data across documents need not be identical but must not conflict; addresses need only sit in the same country; a document may be dated before the credit but not after presentation.
articles.title: Standard for examination of documents
articles.summary: The standard banks apply when examining documents.

articles.read: The invoice appears to be issued by the beneficiary, is made out to the applicant, is in the currency of the credit, and describes the goods in a way that corresponds to the credit. It need not be signed.
articles.title: Commercial invoice
articles.summary: What a commercial invoice must show.

articles.read: A bill of lading, however named, must indicate the name of the carrier and be signed by the carrier or a named agent for the carrier, or by the master or a named agent for the master. Any signature by an agent must indicate whether it signed for the carrier or for the master. It must indicate that the goods have been shipped on board a named vessel at the port of loading stated in the credit, either by pre-printed wording or by an on-board notation giving the date of shipment. It must be the sole original, or where issued in more than one original, the full set as indicated on the bill of lading.
articles.title: Bill of lading
articles.summary: Requirements for a bill of lading.

articles.read: An insurance document must appear to be issued and signed by an insurance company, an underwriter or their agents or proxies. Any signature by an agent or proxy must indicate whether it signed for the insurance company or the underwriter. Where the document indicates it was issued in more than one original, all originals must be presented. Cover notes are not accepted. Cover must be dated no later than shipment unless it shows cover effective from shipment, be in the currency of the credit, and be for at least 110% of the CIF or CIP value.
articles.title: Insurance document and coverage
articles.summary: Insurance documents and the level of cover.

articles.read: If the expiry date or last day for presentation falls on a day the bank is closed for reasons other than force majeure, it extends to the first following banking day; the shipment-to-presentation period is not extended this way.
articles.title: Extension of expiry date
articles.summary: When the last day falls on a closed day.

articles.read: Banks assume no liability for business interrupted by acts of God, riots, wars or other causes beyond their control, and will not honour or negotiate under a credit that expired during such an interruption.
articles.title: Force majeure

articles.read: A credit can be transferred, in whole or part, to a second beneficiary only when it is expressly stated to be transferable. The transferred credit keeps the original terms except for permitted reductions in amount, unit price, expiry, presentation period and latest shipment.
articles.title: Transferable credits
Interpretations
articles.summary: What counts as a signature, and what 'on or about' and similar wordings mean.
articles.read: A document may be signed by handwriting, facsimile signature, perforated signature, stamp, symbol or any other mechanical or electronic method of authentication. A requirement for a document to be legalised, visaed or certified is satisfied by any signature, mark, stamp or label on it that appears to satisfy that requirement.

articles.title: Original documents and copies
articles.summary: At least one original of every stipulated document must be presented.
articles.read: At least one original of each document stipulated in the credit must be presented. A document bearing an apparently original signature, mark, stamp or label of its issuer is treated as an original unless it says otherwise. Unless a document indicates otherwise, a bank accepts it as original if it appears written, typed, perforated or stamped by the issuer's hand, appears on the issuer's original stationery, or states that it is original.

articles.title: On deck, shipper's load and count, freight
articles.summary: Freight prepaid or collect, and clauses disclaiming the carrier's knowledge.
articles.read: A transport document must not indicate that the goods are or will be loaded on deck. A clause stating that the goods may be loaded on deck is acceptable. A transport document bearing a clause such as 'shipper's load and count' or 'said by shipper to contain' is acceptable. A transport document may bear a reference, by stamp or otherwise, to charges additional to the freight.

articles.title: Clean transport document
articles.summary: No clause expressly declaring a defective condition of goods or packaging.
articles.read: A bank will only accept a clean transport document. A clean transport document is one bearing no clause or notation expressly declaring a defective condition of the goods or their packaging. The word 'clean' need not appear on the document, even if the credit has a requirement for that transport document to be 'clean on board'.
Covers how to treat abbreviations, corrections, dates, spelling slips and the meaning of common terms, so examiners apply consistent judgement rather than mechanical matching.
articles.title: General principles of examination

articles.read: Detailed guidance on dating, consignee and notify parties, on-board notations and clean documents when examining bills of lading and other transport documents.
articles.title: Transport document practice
Signatures
articles.summary: A signature need not be handwritten, and a signing capacity must be stated where required.
articles.read: A document may be signed by handwriting, facsimile signature, perforated signature, stamp, symbol or any mechanical or electronic method of authentication. A requirement for a document to be signed is satisfied by any of these. Where a document is signed by a person acting for a named party, the capacity in which it is signed must appear on the document when the applicable article or the credit requires it. A signature on a company's letterhead is taken to be that company's signature unless the document indicates otherwise.

articles.title: Corrections and alterations
articles.summary: A correction on a document not issued by the beneficiary must appear authenticated.
articles.read: Corrections and alterations of information or data in a document, other than in a document issued by the beneficiary, must appear to be authenticated by the party who issued the document or by a party authorised by it. Corrections in a document that has been legalised, visaed or certified must appear to be authenticated by the party that legalised, visaed or certified it. Corrections in a document issued by the beneficiary, other than a draft, need not be authenticated.
